items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, that's who that is, my buddy, boy.

ctx.x: And you grew up hearing music in your home, then, with your mother playing the piano at the church and having these recordings?

Well, like the -- the record that she had. Especially when I was in my teens, because my uncle, my Uncle Louie worked for -- for the relief people. You know, the -- the -- I forget what you call them, but you know, on relief. You know, the relief people, the relief worker. So ­ - let's see now. Why am I saying that? The relief worker. Oh! So they -- they build these new housing projects and he had some pull, so he got us in this new housing project which was called Pennington Court [phonetic sp.]. Brand new. It…
that's okay. But I mean, it just didn't -- it wasn't my cup of tea or coffee, or.
